FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bouillabaisse
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a fisherman's soup: {0_coll} boiled hard with {1_coll} and {2_coll}, the broth served first and the flesh afterwards.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: pissaladière
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a Niçois tart: {0_coll} stewed a whole hour until they are almost a jam, spread over the dough and latticed with {1_adj}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tapenade
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll}, {1_coll} and {2_coll} crushed in a mortar into a black, salt paste. The name comes from the capers, which we do not have.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: daube provençale
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} marinated a whole night, then cooked so long and so gently that it falls apart under the spoon.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: soupe au pistou
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a thick soup of {0_adj} and {1_adj}, into which, off the heat, goes a paste of {2_adj} pounded with oil. The heat of the broth is enough to wake it up.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: bœuf bourguignon
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} braised for hours in {1_plur}, with {2_coll}, until the sauce coats the spoon and the meat gives way without a knife.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: œufs en meurette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached not in water but in a sauce reduced from {1_plur} and {2_plur}, which stains them violet.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gougères
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: choux pastry made with {0_plur}, puffed in the oven until it sounds hollow. Eaten warm, standing up, while waiting for the rest.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: tartiflette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {2_coll} covered over with {1_adj} cut along its length, rind downwards, and put in the oven until everything runs into everything else.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: fondue savoyarde
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} melted in {1_plur} in a pot rubbed with garlic, kept hot the whole evening. Bread is dipped in on the end of a fork; whoever drops it buys the next round.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: aligot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a mash of {0_adj} worked with {1_plur} and a spatula, for a long time, until it draws into ribbons when it is lifted. The arm gives out before the paste does.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: truffade
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} fried in {2_plur}, crushed roughly in the pan and bound with young {1_plur}, without ever leaving the heat.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: potée auvergnate
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {1_coll} and {0_coll} in the same pot, with {2_coll}, stewed half a day. The broth is drunk first, the rest eaten after.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: choucroute garnie
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} salted and left to ferment for weeks, then cooked in {1_plur} and served with {2_plur}. The acidity finishes all the work the salt began.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: baeckeoffe
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {1_coll} stacked in layers, moistened with {2_adj}, the terrine sealed with a rope of dough. It was carried to the baker in the morning and waited in his oven until evening.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: flammekueche
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough rolled out to the very edge of tearing, covered with raw {1_adj} and {2_adj}, slid for two minutes as close to the embers as it will go.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kougelhopf
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a slow brioche baked in a fluted mould, with {1_plur} soaked in advance and {2_plur} set in the bottom so that they end up at the summit.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: buckwheat galette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a {0_adj} batter spread with a rozell over the scorching stone, filled with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, the four corners folded over the yolk while it is still running.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: far breton
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dense custard of {1_plur} and {2_plur}, baked until the top browns and the middle still trembles.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: kouign-amann
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a dough folded and folded again over {1_plur} and {2_plur} until it holds almost as much of them as of flour. The sugar at the bottom caramelises and sticks to the tin; that is the best piece.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: cotriade
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: the sailor's share: the {0_coll} that will not be sold, cooked with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, the broth poured over stale bread.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: garbure
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: a soup so thick with {0_adj}, {1_adj} and {2_adj} that the spoon stands up in it. That is the test, and it is not open to negotiation.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} confit
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} salted for a day, then cooked very slowly submerged in {1_plur}, and kept in it afterwards. The skin is crisped at the last moment, in a pan.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: poule au pot
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} poached whole with {1_coll} and {2_coll}. Henri IV promised one a week to every family; history does not say whether he kept his word.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} blanquette
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} cooked without taking any colour — that is the whole difficulty — the sauce mounted with {1_plur} and sharpened at the very last moment.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gratinéed onion soup
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} browned very slowly to a deep colour, moistened, then covered with bread and {1_adj} and run under the grill.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: croque-monsieur
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: two slices of bread, {2_coll} between them, {1_coll} above and below, the whole browned until the edges run over and catch a little.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: quiche lorraine
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} beaten with {1_plur} and poured over {2_coll} taken in the pan, in a shortcrust case. There is no cheese in it, whatever anyone says.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: coq au vin
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} from a bird too old for anything else, saved by a long cooking in {1_plur}, with {2_coll}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: rabbit with mustard
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} painted over with {2_adj} before it goes in, the sauce deglazed and bound with {1_plur}. The mustard loses its heat and keeps only its acidity.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: gratin dauphinois
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} in fine slices, cooked in {1_plur} in a dish rubbed with {2_adj}. The starch is enough to bind it; there is no cheese, and that is not an oversight.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: {0_adj} brandade
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} soaked out then worked up with oil into a paste, loosened with {1_plur} and lifted with {2_plur}.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: carbonade flamande
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} and {2_coll} stewed long in {1_plur}, softened with a little sugar and a slice of mustarded bread that dissolves into the sauce.

FlavorText.FlavorDef.label: moules marinière
FlavorText.FlavorDef.description: {0_coll} opened over a high flame with {1_plur} and {2_plur}, in its own liquor. The ones that stay shut are thrown away.
